note: The armed weapon in Dink's hand (bug A203): 1997 reloads Dink's idle, walk and attack sequences with the weapon's pictures while it is armed (item-sw1.c graphics\dink\sword\..., item-b1.c graphics\dink\bow\...), so the remaster attaches the weapon mesh to his hand for as long as the item's script is the armed weapon. Meshes and grip transforms from the art kit HeroWeapons (PR #157; origin at the grip centre, +X to the tip): swords and axe on hand_r at (-7, 3, -0.5) cm, pitch 90 yaw 0 roll 90; bows on hand_l at (7, -3, 0.5) cm, pitch -90 yaw 0 roll 90. Fists (item-fst) and the bomb carry nothing. Read by UDinkHeroWeaponSubsystem (DinkHeroWeapon.h).

bows.note: The bow that bends, its arrow and the quiver (art row AN-05). 1997 draws the armed bow with an arrow across it and a quiver of red-fletched arrows on Dink's back (graphics\dink\bow\idle, walk), and the bow bending while it is drawn (bow\hit). The bow items' hand mesh above is the bow's middle part; `parts` names the others (%s = LimbU1.., LimbL1.., StringU, StringL; art kit HeroWeapons, tools/build_bow_parts.py, which prints `draw`). Centimetres in the bow mesh's axes: X up the upper limb, +Y from the grip to the string. While the bow is drawn the string is pulled to where the body's `string_fingers` are (their middle), at the arrow's height `nock_up_cm`, as long as they are within `follow_cm` [all, none] of the string's line; each limb's segments turn about `joints_cm` by `weights` of the bend that keeps the string's length. `arrow`: its nock on the string, its shaft `rest_z_cm` to the side of the stave, away for `away_after_shot_s` after a shot. `worn`: the quiver on a body bone, as an item row. Read by UDinkHeroBowSubsystem (DinkHeroBow.h).
